title: Rave Master
synopsis: A boy wielding a sword of holy stones sets out with a strange little dog to destroy the dark stones that threaten the world, in Hiro Mashima's first series. The title reduces to 5 — the turn.
body:
5Filed under 5. The Turn takes a turn, and this entry is changes one.

What it is

Hiro Mashima's Rave Master, published in Japan as Rave, and whose anime was called Groove Adventure Rave, ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 1999 to 2005 and was collected in thirty-five volumes. It was Mashima's first serialisation.

The story

Haru Glory is a cheerful boy living on a quiet island with his sister. He meets an old man, Shiba, the last Rave Master, and his companion Plue, a small, white, trembling creature with a carrot nose. Shiba passes on the Ten Commandments sword and the power of the holy stones called Rave, and Haru sets out to find the scattered Rave stones and destroy the evil Dark Bring stones used by the criminal empire Demon Card.

The style

It is an energetic, warm fantasy adventure full of comedy, friendship and transforming swords. Many of its ideas and character types were developed further in Mashima's Fairy Tail.

Why it matters

It launched Mashima's career, and its characters still appear in his later series. It was adapted into an anime in 2001.

How the story is divided

The early volumes follow Haru's departure from his island with Plue and the clumsy, cheerful Elie, a girl with no memory of her past, and their first fights with Demon Card. The middle of the series is a war against Demon Card's leader, King, and then against the young emperor Lucia, his son, as Haru gathers the Rave stones one by one. The final volumes reveal the truth about Elie, about the catastrophe that created the Dark Bring stones fifty years before, and about the being behind it all.

Adaptations

Studio Deen's anime, Groove Adventure Rave, ran for 51 episodes in 2001 and 2002, ending well before the manga.

Reading it today

Complete in 35 volumes. Readers who came to Mashima through Fairy Tail will find many of its ideas here first. Our entry on Hiro Mashima covers his other works.

title: Fire Force
synopsis: In a Tokyo where people burst into flames and become monsters, a young firefighter with burning feet joins a special brigade that fights them. 58 in the letters, reducing to 4.
body:
4Reduced, this title gives 4. It sits on The Structure with the rest of a structure.

What it is

Atsushi Ōkubo's Fire Force ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2015 to 2022 and was collected in thirty-four volumes. In an alternative Tokyo, people suddenly combust and turn into Infernals, burning monsters. Special fire brigades, run partly as a religious order, put them to rest.

The story

Shinra Kusakabe is a third-generation pyrokinetic who can ignite fire from his feet and fly. People call him "devil" for his nervous grin and because, as a child, he was blamed for the fire that took his mother and baby brother. He joins Special Fire Force Company 8 to become a hero and to learn the truth about that fire, and discovers a conspiracy behind the combustions.

The style

Ōkubo's art is sharp and stylised, with striking designs and explosive action. The series combines firefighting, religion and conspiracy, and grows into a cosmic story.

Why it matters

It is Ōkubo's second major work after Soul Eater, and its ending reveals a link between the two. It was adapted into an anime from 2019.

How the story is divided

The early volumes introduce Company 8 and its members, Captain Obi, the pyrokinetic Maki, the self-styled knight Arthur and the nun Iris, as they investigate whether the other companies are hiding the truth about the Infernals. The middle of the series uncovers the Evangelist, a figure behind the combustions, and the search for the Pillars, people with a rare power called the Adolla Burst. The final volumes are a cosmic catastrophe that remakes the world, and the last chapters reveal how it connects to Ōkubo's earlier Soul Eater.

Adaptations

David Production's anime began in 2019, with a second season in 2020 and a third, final season from 2025. Readers who know Soul Eater should read Fire Force to the end: the connection between the two is one of the most surprising endings in recent shōnen.

title: Neuro: Supernatural Detective
synopsis: A demon who feeds on mysteries uses a high-school girl as the public face of his detective work, in Yūsei Matsui's dark and very strange comedy. Read from the ledger, as an 8.
body:
8Filed under 8. The Ledger takes a reckoning, and this entry is commands one.

What it is

Yūsei Matsui's Neuro ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2005 to 2009 and was collected in twenty-three volumes. Neuro Nōgami is a demon who feeds on the "mysteries" produced by crimes, and has eaten all the mysteries of the demon world. He comes to the human world to find more.

The story

He chooses Yako Katsuragi, a high-school girl whose father has just been murdered, as his front. Every time he solves a case, he makes Yako announce the answer, so that she becomes a famous teenage detective against her will. Neuro torments her constantly, and slowly grows to respect her.

The style

It is a detective story, a horror comedy and a parody all at once. Its killers have grotesque, exaggerated designs and "true selves" that burst out when they are exposed, and Neuro's demonic tools are absurd and frightening.

Why it matters

It was Matsui's first serialisation, and its blend of humour and darkness carried into Assassination Classroom. It was adapted into an anime in 2007.

How the story is divided

The early volumes are separate cases, each with a murderer whose true self erupts when Neuro unmasks him. The first long arc is the hunt for X, a phantom thief who changes his body at will and kills to understand what he really is. The final arcs set Neuro and Yako against Six and the New Bloodline, a group of criminals who claim to be a new species of humanity, and the story turns to whether Neuro, weakened by the human world, can survive it.

Adaptations

Madhouse's anime (2007–2008) adapted the early arcs and then told its own ending.

title: Love Hina
synopsis: A young man who keeps failing the Tokyo University entrance exam ends up managing a girls' dormitory, in the romantic comedy that defined its era. The title reduces to 5 — the turn.
body:
5A 5 by its title: freedom seeker, and therefore the turn.

What it is

Ken Akamatsu's Love Hina ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 1998 to 2001 and was collected in fourteen volumes. Keitarō Urashima once promised a girl, when they were children, that they would both go to Tokyo University. He no longer remembers her name, and he has failed the entrance exam twice.

The story

Thrown out of his home, he goes to his grandmother's inn, Hinata-sō, and finds that it has become a dormitory for girls. Through a series of accidents, he becomes its manager. He studies for a third attempt, while slowly falling for Naru Narusegawa, a fierce student who is also aiming for Tokyo University.

The style

It is a romantic comedy with a large cast of heroines, slapstick, misunderstandings and a good deal of fanservice. Under the comedy is a story about failure and trying again.

Why it matters

It was one of the most influential romantic comedies around 2000, and helped set the formula for the multiple-heroine love story. It was adapted into an anime in 2000 and was a big early hit in English.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are the comedy of Keitarō's arrival at Hinata-sō and his failed third attempt at the entrance exam. The middle of the series sends him and Naru on a trip abroad, and to an archaeological dig, and he begins to find a life outside the exam. The last volumes bring the promise from his childhood into the open, settle the romance, and give the long-promised entrance exam its result.

Adaptations

Xebec's anime ran for 24 episodes in 2000, followed by television specials and an OVA, Love Hina Again (2002). In English it was one of the first manga to sell widely in bookshops, in Tokyopop's edition.

Reading it today

Complete in 14 volumes. Our guide to romantic comedy in manga places it in the line from Maison Ikkoku to The Quintessential Quintuplets.

title: Negima! Magister Negi Magi
synopsis: A ten-year-old wizard from Wales is sent to teach English to a class of thirty-one schoolgirls in Japan, and the comedy slowly becomes a fantasy epic. Read from the ledger, as an 8.
body:
8Eight — power. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Ken Akamatsu's Negima! ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2003 to 2012 and was collected in thirty-eight volumes. Negi Springfield is a ten-year-old wizard from Wales. As the final test of his training, he is sent to Mahora Academy in Japan to teach English to a class of thirty-one girls.

The story

He must keep his magic secret, which goes wrong immediately. As he gets to know his pupils, many of them turn out to have secrets of their own, and some become his partners in magical contracts. Negi is also searching for his father, the legendary wizard known as the Thousand Master.

The change

The series begins as a romantic comedy like Akamatsu's Love Hina, but over time it becomes a full battle fantasy, with tournaments, a trip to the magic world and a huge, detailed magic system.

Why it matters

It is the clearest case of a series changing genre in mid-run, from harem comedy to full battle fantasy, without abandoning its cast. It was adapted into anime and continued in the sequel UQ Holder!.

How the story is divided

The early volumes are school comedy in Mahora Academy, with Negi's first contract and a class trip to Kyoto that turns into his first real battle. The series then moves into longer arcs: a fight with the vampire Evangeline, who becomes his teacher; the Mahora Festival, with its martial-arts tournament and a student who plans to reveal magic to the world; and the Magic World arc, in which Negi and his students are trapped in another world and the truth about his parents comes out.

Adaptations and sequel

Two different anime were made, Negima! (2005) and Negima!? (2006), neither following the manga far, and a film, Anime Final, followed in 2011. The sequel UQ Holder! (2013–2022), set decades later, ran for 28 volumes and was adapted as an anime in 2017.

title: Natsume's Book of Friends
synopsis: A lonely boy who can see spirits inherits his grandmother's book of the yōkai she defeated, and sets out to return their names. 89 in the letters, reducing to 8.
body:
8Reduced, this title gives 8. It sits on The Ledger with the rest of a reckoning.

What it is

Yuki Midorikawa's Natsume's Book of Friends began in Hakusensha's LaLa DX in 2003 and moved to LaLa in 2008. Takashi Natsume is an orphaned high-school student who has always been able to see yōkai, which made him a strange, lonely child passed between relatives.

The story

Now living with a kind couple in the countryside, he finds his late grandmother Reiko's Book of Friends. Reiko, as lonely as he was, beat yōkai in contests and made them write their names in the book, which binds them to the owner. Takashi decides to give the names back, one by one. He is protected by Madara, a powerful spirit who usually takes the form of a fat, lucky cat and is called Nyanko-sensei.

The tone

Each story brings a yōkai with its own longing or grief. The series is gentle, melancholy and often funny, and about kindness, memory and learning to let people in.

Why it matters

It is one of the best-loved supernatural manga, and a model of the quiet, iyashikei kind of yōkai story. Its anime, which began in 2008, has run for many seasons.

How the story is divided

There is no single arc: most stories are one to three chapters, each about one yōkai and its name in the book. A few threads run through the whole series, including the exorcist Natori, who works with yōkai for money, and the powerful and ruthless Matoba clan of exorcists, whose head wants Takashi's power for his own ends; the story of Reiko herself, revealed in small fragments; and Takashi's growing trust in his foster family and friends.

Adaptations

The anime, by Brain's Base and later Shuka, has run for seven seasons, from 2008 to 2024, with two films, Ephemeral Bond (2018) and The Waking Rock and the Strange Visitor (2021). The manga has passed 33 volumes and 16 million copies.

Reading it today

It can be read in any order and at any pace, a few chapters at a time. Our guide to slice of life and iyashikei places it among the quiet stories it resembles.

title: The Flowers of Evil
synopsis: A bookish boy steals the gym clothes of the girl he worships, and a classmate who saw him forces him into a contract to tear his life apart. The title reduces to 11 — the signal.
body:
11An 11 by its title: visionary (master 11), and therefore the signal.

What it is

Shūzō Oshimi's The Flowers of Evil ran in Kodansha's Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine from 2009 to 2014 and was collected in eleven volumes. Takao Kasuga is a middle-school student in a small town surrounded by mountains. He loves Baudelaire's Les Fleurs du mal and believes it makes him different from everyone else.

The story

One day, alone in the classroom, he steals the gym clothes of Nanako Saeki, the girl he idolises. Sawa Nakamura, an angry, isolated classmate, saw him do it. Instead of telling anyone, she forces him into a "contract": he must show her the pervert she believes he really is. Their relationship pulls in Saeki and escalates in disturbing ways.

Two halves

The second half jumps forward to high school, where Kasuga, now in a new town, struggles to live with what he did. It becomes a quiet story about recovery and growing up.

Why it matters

It is a powerful, uncomfortable portrait of adolescent shame, desire and the wish to escape. Its 2013 anime was made with rotoscoping, and it was also adapted into a live-action film.

How the story is divided

The first half, the middle-school arc, follows Kasuga's contract with Nakamura, its escalation into vandalism and running away, and an attempt to escape the town that ends in disaster. The second half, the high-school arc, takes place years later in another town, where Kasuga meets Tokiwa, a girl who writes fiction, and has to face Saeki and Nakamura again before he can move on.

Adaptations

Zexcs' 2013 anime, made with rotoscoping, adapted only the beginning of the first half. A live-action film in 2019 adapted both halves.

Reading it today

Complete in eleven volumes. Readers who stopped with the anime should start the manga from the beginning, since the anime stops early and the manga's art is very different.

title: Teasing Master Takagi-san
altTitles: からかい上手の高木さん
synopsis: A middle-school girl teases the boy beside her every day, and he never manages to get her back, in a gentle comedy of first love. The title reduces to 9 — the closing.
body:
9Filed under 9. The Closing takes a completion, and this entry is hands on one.

What it is

Sōichirō Yamamoto's Teasing Master Takagi-san ran in Shogakukan's Monthly Shōnen Sunday from 2013 to 2023 and was collected in twenty volumes. Nishikata sits next to Takagi in class. Every day she teases him, and every day he swears he will get his revenge.

How it works

Each short chapter is a small contest: a bet, a trick, a game or a misunderstanding. Nishikata always loses, because Takagi reads him perfectly. Readers can see what he cannot, that she teases him because she likes him.

The tone

It is gentle and small in scale, set in a quiet seaside town, with very little drama. The comedy is in the timing and in Nishikata's red-faced defeats, and the romance moves very slowly.

Why it matters

It was a big hit and helped popularise the "teasing" romantic comedy. It was adapted into an anime in 2018 and an anime film in 2022, and a spin-off shows Takagi as an adult, married to Nishikata.

How the story moves

The series takes Takagi and Nishikata through their three years of middle school, and time passes slowly but really: seasons change, festivals and summer holidays come round, and their relationship deepens in steps so small that each one feels like an event. It is best read a few chapters at a time, the way it was published.

Adaptations and spin-offs

The anime ran for three seasons (2018, 2019 and 2022) and concluded with a film in 2022. A live-action television series and film followed in 2024. The spin-off Karakai Jōzu no (Moto) Takagi-san, drawn by Mifumi Inaba, shows Takagi as an adult, married to Nishikata and raising their daughter, and still teasing him. Yamamoto's later comedies, such as Soredemo Ayumu wa Yosetekuru, apply the same formula to a shogi club.

title: Dororo
synopsis: A young swordsman whose body parts were traded to demons before his birth hunts them down to win himself back, with a child thief at his side. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4Four — foundation. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Osamu Tezuka's Dororo began in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday in 1967 and later continued in Bōken'ō. It is set in Japan's Warring States period, a time of war, famine and monsters.

The story

To gain power, the samurai lord Kagemitsu Daigo promises forty-eight demons that each may take a part of his unborn son's body. The baby is born without limbs, eyes, ears or skin, and is set adrift on a river. A doctor finds him and gives him artificial body parts, including arms that hide swords. As a young man, Hyakkimaru sets out to kill the demons; with each death, a part of his body returns.

Dororo

He is joined by Dororo, a bold, foul-mouthed young thief who wants his swords. Their friendship, and Dororo's own secret, are the warm heart of a grim story about war, poverty and what makes a person whole.

Why it matters

It is one of Tezuka's darkest adventures and an ancestor of many later stories of cursed heroes and demon hunting. It was adapted into anime in 1969 and again in 2019.

How it is organised

The story is a series of encounters, as Hyakkimaru and Dororo travel through a war-ravaged country and fight the demons who hold his body parts. Each fight returns something: his voice, his ears, his legs. The later chapters bring Hyakkimaru back to his father's domain and his younger brother Tahōmaru, and set him against the family that sacrificed him. Tezuka ended the series early, and many demons remain undefeated.

Adaptations

Mushi Production's anime ran in 1969. Tezuka Productions and MAPPA's 2019 remake was widely praised and gave the story a fuller ending. A live-action film appeared in 2007.

Reading it today

Short, and complete despite its abrupt ending. Our entry on Osamu Tezuka covers his other works.

title: Perman
synopsis: An ordinary boy is given a mask, cape and badge by an alien and becomes a secret superhero, with a robot double to cover for him at home. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4Filed under 4. The Structure takes a structure, and this entry is frames one.

What it is

Fujiko F. Fujio's Perman first ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday and children's magazines from 1967, and was revived in the 1980s. Mitsuo Suwa is an ordinary, rather lazy schoolboy.

The story

An alien called Birdman chooses Mitsuo to be a superhero. He gives him a mask that gives him great strength, a cape that lets him fly and a badge for communication. Mitsuo becomes Perman, and to keep his identity secret he is given a Copy Robot, which becomes an exact copy of him when he presses its nose and takes his place at home and at school. He is soon joined by other Permen, including a chimpanzee.

The style

Like Doraemon, it is a gentle comedy about an imperfect boy and the problems that magical tools bring. Being a hero is hard work, and Mitsuo would often rather sleep.

Why it matters

It is one of Fujiko F. Fujio's best-loved works after Doraemon, and a Japanese answer to the American superhero. It was adapted into anime in 1967 and 1983.

How it is organised

Each chapter is a self-contained episode, either a rescue, a mishap with the Copy Robot or a clash between Mitsuo's two lives. Other Permen join him: a chimpanzee, Booby; Pako, who is secretly the idol singer Sumire Hoshino; Pāyan, a boy from Osaka; and Pābō, a baby. In the original ending, Mitsuo is called to Birdman's planet to train, and leaves his friends and Pako behind.

Adaptations

The first anime, in black and white, ran in 1967 and 1968, and the second from 1983 to 1987, with films.

Reading it today

It reads well at any age, and its gentle comedy is close to Doraemon. Our entry on Fujiko F. Fujio covers his other works.

title: Cutie Honey
synopsis: An android girl who can transform into any identity fights a gang of female villains to avenge her father, in Go Nagai's influential action heroine story. Filed under 8, the ledger.
body:
8Reduced, this title gives 8. It sits on The Ledger with the rest of a reckoning.

What it is

Go Nagai's Cutie Honey ran in Akita Shoten's Weekly Shōnen Champion in 1973 and 1974, alongside its television anime by Toei. Honey Kisaragi is a cheerful schoolgirl at a strict Catholic boarding school. She is also an android, built by her scientist father.

The story

When her father is murdered by Panther Claw, a criminal organisation of women seeking the device inside Honey that can create matter from the air, she sets out for revenge. With the cry "Honey Flash!", she can transform into any form she likes, from a reporter to a biker, and above all into Cutie Honey, a red-haired warrior with a sword.

The style

It is fast, violent, comic and openly sexy, typical of Nagai, with transformations that reveal Honey for a moment between costumes.

Why it matters

Honey was one of the first action heroines in anime and manga aimed at boys. Her transformation sequence was an ancestor of the magical-girl transformations of Sailor Moon and many others, and the story has been remade many times, including a live-action film in 2004.

How it is organised

Each chapter sets Honey against a new member of Panther Claw, a gang of fantastic villainesses led by Sister Jill. Honey's school, her suspicious headmistress and the comic Hayami family, a journalist, his father and his young brother, who help her, provide the comedy between fights. The manga's story ends quickly, but Honey has returned in many later versions.

Adaptations

Toei's anime (1973–1974) was the first of many. Later versions include the OVA New Cutie Honey (1994), Cutie Honey Flash (1997), aimed at girls after Sailor Moon, Hideaki Anno's live-action film (2004) and Re: Cutie Honey (2004), and Cutie Honey Universe (2018).

Reading it today

It is short. Readers interested in the history of the magical girl can see in it the transformation sequence that later shōjo series made their own. Our glossary entry on magical girls traces that line, and our entry on Go Nagai covers his other works.

title: Reborn!
synopsis: A hopeless schoolboy discovers he is the heir to a powerful mafia family, and is trained to lead it by a hitman who looks like a baby. 36 in the letters, reducing to 9.
body:
9Reduced, this title gives 9. It sits on The Closing with the rest of a completion.

What it is

Akira Amano's Reborn! ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2004 to 2012 and was collected in forty-two volumes. Tsunayoshi Sawada, known as "No-Good Tsuna", is a middle-school student who is bad at studying, sport and everything else.

The story

One day a hitman arrives at his house as his new home tutor. Reborn looks like an infant in a suit, but he is one of the best killers in the world, sent by the ninth boss of the Italian mafia family Vongola. Tsuna, it turns out, is the family's heir. Reborn's training method is to shoot him with a Dying Will Bullet, which makes him try with all his might to do whatever he regretted not doing.

The change

The series begins as a gag comedy and gradually becomes a battle manga, with Tsuna's school friends as his guardians and fights against rival families, including a long arc in the future.

Why it matters

It was one of Jump's most popular series of the 2000s, with a large following for its characters. It was adapted into an anime from 2006 to 2010.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are gag comedy: Reborn's training, and the gathering of Tsuna's future guardians, among them the hot-headed Gokudera, the baseball player Yamamoto and the cold disciplinary committee head Hibari. The battle manga begins with the Kokuyo arc, against the escaped convict Mukuro, and the Varia arc, in which Tsuna's guardians fight the Vongola's assassination squad, one-on-one, for the right to inherit the rings. The longest arc sends them ten years into the future, where a rival family, the Millefiore, is hunting the Vongola, and the last arcs turn to the curse that made Reborn and the other Arcobaleno infants.

Adaptations

Artland's anime ran for 203 episodes from 2006 to 2010 and stops during the future arc.

title: Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan
synopsis: A boy who is one quarter yōkai is heir to his grandfather's great clan of spirits, and must choose between his human life and leading the night parade. Read from the inquiry, as a 7.
body:
7Filed under 7. The Inquiry takes an open question, and this entry is examines one.

What it is

Hiroshi Shiibashi's Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2008 to 2012 and was collected in twenty-five volumes. Rikuo Nura is a cheerful, helpful middle-school student. He is also the grandson of Nurarihyon, the supreme commander of the yōkai, and one quarter yōkai himself.

The story

By day, Rikuo wants only to be human, and hides his family from his school friends, one of whom is obsessed with finding yōkai. At night, his yōkai blood takes over and he becomes a cool, commanding figure. His grandfather's Nura clan wants him as its next leader, and rival clans want to destroy it.

Its folklore

The series is full of figures from Japanese folklore, from the snow woman Yuki-onna to kappa and karasu-tengu, and later travels to Kyoto to face older and more dangerous yōkai, as well as onmyōji.

Why it matters

It is a lively example of the yōkai battle manga in Jump, and was adapted into anime in 2010 and 2011.

How the story is divided

The first arcs follow Rikuo's double life and his first fights as heir, against rival clans in his own territory and against the Shikoku yōkai, who want to take over the Nura clan's lands. The longest arc is the journey to Kyoto, where Rikuo and his followers fight to stop the resurrection of Hagoromo-Gitsune, a legendary fox, alongside the onmyōji of the Keikain family. The last arc turns to the Hundred Stories clan, which creates new yōkai out of urban legends, and to the enemy behind Rikuo's father's death.

Adaptations

The anime ran for two seasons, Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan (2010) and Demon Capital (2011), which adapted the Kyoto arc.

title: Fushigi Yūgi
synopsis: A schoolgirl is pulled into an ancient Chinese book and becomes the priestess of a god, searching for seven warriors while her best friend becomes her enemy. 69 in the letters, reducing to 6.
body:
6Reduced, this title gives 6. It sits on The Care with the rest of an obligation.

What it is

Yuu Watase's Fushigi Yūgi, "Mysterious Play", ran in Shogakukan's Shōjo Comic from 1992 to 1996 and was collected in eighteen volumes. Miaka Yūki is a cheerful, hungry middle-school student studying for her high-school entrance exams.

The story

In a library, Miaka and her best friend Yui find an old book, The Universe of the Four Gods, and are pulled into its world, a kingdom modelled on ancient China. Miaka becomes the Priestess of Suzaku. To summon the god and have her wish granted, she must gather his seven Celestial Warriors, among them Tamahome, with whom she falls in love. Yui, hurt and abandoned, becomes the Priestess of the rival god Seiryū.

The style

It mixes romance, comedy, adventure and real tragedy, with many characters' deaths. It was one of the most important early stories of a girl transported into another world, long before isekai became a genre.

Why it matters

It was a great hit for shōjo manga in the 1990s and a popular anime from 1995. Watase later wrote a prequel, Fushigi Yūgi: Genbu Kaiden.

How the story is divided

The first part follows Miaka's arrival in the kingdom of Konan, her love for Tamahome and the gathering of the Suzaku warriors, while Yui, abandoned in the book, turns against her. The second part is a war with the Seiryū warriors of the rival kingdom of Kutō, as the two priestesses race to summon their gods. The last volumes, after the summoning, take the story back to the modern world, where the book's power follows Miaka and Tamahome.

Adaptations and prequels

Pierrot's anime ran for 52 episodes from 1995 to 1996, and two OVA series followed, the second adapting the final volumes that the series left out. Watase wrote two prequels about earlier priestesses: Fushigi Yūgi: Genbu Kaiden (2003–2013) and Byakko Senki, which began in 2017. The series has passed 20 million copies in circulation.

title: Vampire Knight
synopsis: At an academy where vampires secretly study alongside humans, a girl with no memory of her early childhood is caught between two very different young men. Filed under 9, the closing.
body:
9Title sums to 72 and reduces to 9 — The Closing, where the reference files a completion.

What it is

Matsuri Hino's Vampire Knight ran in Hakusensha's LaLa from 2004 to 2013 and was collected in nineteen volumes. Cross Academy has two classes: the Day Class, of ordinary students, and the Night Class, of beautiful elite students who are, in secret, vampires.

The story

Yūki Cross, the headmaster's adopted daughter, remembers nothing before the night, ten years ago, when a vampire attacked her and the pureblood vampire Kaname Kuran saved her. Now she is a guardian who keeps the two classes apart, together with Zero Kiryū, a boy whose family was killed by a vampire and who hates them all. Yūki is drawn to both Kaname and Zero, and her lost memories hold the key to everything.

The style

It is a gothic romance, full of elegant uniforms, blood, secrets and longing, drawn in an ornate style.

Why it matters

It was one of the most popular shōjo manga of the 2000s, especially in English, and helped define a wave of vampire romance. It was adapted into anime in 2008, and Hino later continued it with a sequel set years later.

How the story is divided

The early volumes are a gothic school romance, as Yūki guards the Night Class and Zero struggles against becoming a vampire himself. The middle of the series reveals Yūki's lost past, which changes everything about her relationship with Kaname. The last volumes leave the academy behind and become a war among vampires and between vampires and hunters, ending in a choice that divided readers.

Adaptations and sequel

Studio Deen's anime ran for two seasons in 2008, Vampire Knight and Vampire Knight Guilty, and covers about half of the story with its own ending. Hino continued the story in Vampire Knight: Memories, set after the original ending, which ran in LaLa DX from 2016 to 2025 and was collected in 11 volumes.

title: Phantom Thief Jeanne
synopsis: A schoolgirl who is the reincarnation of Joan of Arc becomes a phantom thief, stealing paintings possessed by demons. Filed under 4, the structure.
body:
4Title sums to 85 and reduces to 4 — The Structure, where the reference files a structure.

What it is

Arina Tanemura's Phantom Thief Jeanne ran in Shueisha's Ribon from 1998 to 2000 and was collected in seven volumes. Maron Kusakabe is a high-school gymnast who lives alone, her parents having left her.

The story

Maron is the reincarnation of Joan of Arc, and with the help of a small angel-in-training, Fin, she transforms into the phantom thief Jeanne. Demons have hidden in beautiful paintings and, through them, corrupt the hearts of their owners. Jeanne steals the paintings and seals the demons away, while the police and her best friend, the daughter of the detective chasing her, try to catch her. A rival thief, Sinbad, and a new boy in her building, Chiaki, complicate everything.

The style

Tanemura's art is extremely decorative, with large eyes, flowing hair, ribbons and flowers, and the story grows from a magical-girl romance into a darker tale about loneliness and faith.

Why it matters

It was Tanemura's first big hit and a classic of late 1990s Ribon. It was adapted into anime in 1999.

How the story is divided

The early volumes are heists: each chapter a painting, a demon and a narrow escape from the police and from Sinbad. Midway through, the story reveals who Sinbad really is, and why he and his angel have come to Maron. The last volumes turn to the being behind the demons and to the truth about Fin, and test Maron's faith and her loneliness to the limit.

Adaptations

Toei's anime ran for 44 episodes from 1999 to 2000, with an ending of its own.

Reading it today

Complete in seven volumes. Tanemura's colour pages and ornate layouts reward a large-format edition. Our glossary entry on magical girls explains the genre it belongs to.

title: Bokurano
synopsis: Fifteen children agree to pilot a giant robot to save the Earth, and learn that each battle will cost the pilot their life. The title reduces to 7 — the inquiry.
body:
7Filed under 7. The Inquiry takes an open question, and this entry is searches one.

What it is

Mohiro Kitoh's Bokurano, "Ours", ran in Shogakukan's IKKI from 2003 to 2009 and was collected in eleven volumes. Fifteen children at a summer school camp find a cave by the sea, where a strange man asks them to play a game: to pilot a giant robot and fight enemies to protect the Earth.

The story

They sign his contract, thinking it a game. Then a vast black robot appears off the coast, and enemies begin to arrive. The children learn the rules one by one: each battle is piloted by one child, chosen in turn; the robot is powered by the pilot's life, so the pilot dies after the battle; and if they lose, the Earth is destroyed.

The structure

Each volume follows a different pilot through their last days, their family, their secrets and what they decide matters. The robot's enemies, it turns out, are not monsters.

Why it matters

It is one of manga's bleakest and most powerful answers to the giant robot genre, turning its fantasy of children saving the world into a meditation on death and responsibility. It was adapted into an anime in 2007.

How the story is divided

After the first battles and the death of the first pilots, the series follows each child in turn, and each life reveals a different side of Japan: one pilot spends her last days on revenge, another discovers his family's secrets. The adults, among them the government and the army, try to use the robot, and the children learn the truth about the enemies they are killing. The last pilots face the final battle, and the question of whether their deaths have any meaning.

Adaptations

Gonzo's anime (2007) told its own story, darker in some ways and gentler in others, and ended before the manga did.

Reading it today

Complete in eleven volumes. It is harrowing, and some chapters deal with abuse. Our entry on Narutaru covers Kitoh's earlier series, and our glossary entry on mecha explains the genre it answers.

title: Yaiba
synopsis: A wild boy raised in the jungle to be a samurai comes to Japan and battles a rival who has made himself a demon, in Gosho Aoyama's comic adventure. Filed under 2, the pairing.
body:
2Title sums to 20 and reduces to 2 — The Pairing, where the reference files a negotiation.

What it is

Gosho Aoyama's Yaiba ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday from 1988 to 1993 and was collected in twenty-four volumes, just before Aoyama began Detective Conan. Yaiba Kurogane has grown up in the jungle, trained in swordsmanship by his father, and believes himself a samurai.

The story

He arrives in Japan and moves in with the Mine family, whose daughter Sayaka becomes his companion. He makes an enemy of Takeshi Onimaru, a kendō champion whose pride he hurts. Onimaru takes up a cursed sword, turns into a demon and sets out to conquer Japan, and Yaiba must find the legendary swords of thunder and wind to stop him.

The style

It is a fast, silly and inventive adventure, full of puns, monsters, historical swordsmen and battles that grow ever larger, ending far beyond Japan.

Why it matters

It was Aoyama's first long hit. It was adapted into anime in 1993, and a new anime adaptation was made in 2025.

How the story is divided

The early volumes are Yaiba's arrival in Japan and his rivalry with Onimaru. The story grows into a quest for the legendary swords, the Raijin and Fūjin, and the orbs of the dragon god, and into battles with figures from Japanese history and legend, among them Musashi Miyamoto, who becomes Yaiba's teacher. The final arcs leave Japan altogether, fighting the Eight-Headed Serpent and a war that reaches as far as the moon, where the alien Kaguya is waiting.

Adaptations

The 1993 anime ran for 52 episodes. Wit Studio's Yaiba: Samurai Legend began in April 2025, with a second season covering the Kaguya arc scheduled for January 2027. The manga won the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1993 and has passed 17 million copies.

Reading it today

title: X
synopsis: A young man with great psychic power returns to Tokyo, where two groups of chosen warriors fight over whether humanity will survive the end of the world. 6 in the letters, with nothing left to reduce.
body:
6The letters of this title total 6 outright — the number of care, community, and the weight of duty.

What it is

CLAMP's X, also known as X/1999, ran in Kadokawa's Monthly Asuka from 1992 until it went on hiatus in 2003, with eighteen volumes published. It is CLAMP's most ambitious and darkest apocalyptic epic.

The story

Kamui Shirō returns to Tokyo after six years away, keeping a promise to his late mother. He learns that the end of the world is coming, and that he must choose between two sides: the Dragons of Heaven, who will protect humanity, and the Dragons of Earth, who will destroy it to save the planet. Whichever side he chooses, his childhood friend Fūma will take the other, and Fūma's sister Kotori, whom Kamui loves, is at the centre of their fate.

The style

It is full of tragic destinies, psychic battles and the destruction of Tokyo's landmarks, drawn with CLAMP's elegant figures and dramatic compositions. Characters from Tokyo Babylon and other CLAMP works appear.

Why it matters

Despite being unfinished, it is one of CLAMP's best-known works, with an anime film in 1996 and a television series in 2001.

How the story is divided

The first volumes bring Kamui to Tokyo and introduce the two sides: the Dragons of Heaven, gathered by the dreamseer Hinoto, and the Dragons of Earth, gathered by her sister Kanoe. Kamui's choice, made in a single terrible moment, sets Fūma against him and costs Kotori her life. The rest of the series is a war between the two sets of seals and their opposites across Tokyo, each battle destroying a landmark, a protective "barrier" of the city, and each pair of fighters with their own reasons and losses.

Adaptations

Rintarō's animated film (1996) compressed the story into ninety minutes with its own ending. Madhouse's television series (2001–2002) followed the manga more closely and also invented an ending, since the manga had none.

Reading it today

Eighteen volumes have been published, and the series has been on hiatus since 2003. Readers should know that it stops without an ending. Our entry on CLAMP covers their finished series.

title: Drifters
synopsis: A samurai dying after the battle of Sekigahara wakes in a fantasy world at war, where famous figures from history are fighting on both sides. The title reduces to 9 — the closing.
body:
9Filed under 9. The Closing takes a completion, and this entry is hands on one.

What it is

Kōta Hirano's Drifters has run in Shōnen Gahōsha's Young King OURs since 2009, after Hellsing. Shimazu Toyohisa, a young samurai, is badly wounded in the retreat after the battle of Sekigahara in 1600.

The story

Instead of dying, he finds himself in a strange corridor and is sent into a fantasy world of elves, dwarves and kingdoms. People from history have been brought there too. The Drifters, among them Oda Nobunaga and the archer Nasu no Yoichi, are sent by one mysterious figure; the Ends, among them a vengeful Joan of Arc and Rasputin, are sent by another, and lead an army of monsters to wipe out humanity.

The style

It is wildly violent, funny and full of energy, like Hellsing, and it delights in putting historical figures together: generals, soldiers and outlaws from Japan, Europe and beyond, each with their own tactics.

Why it matters

It is an unusual, adult twist on the isekai idea, built on military history. It was adapted into an anime in 2016.

How the story is divided

The first volumes bring Toyohisa, Nobunaga and Yoichi together in an elf village oppressed by a human kingdom, where they start a rebellion and begin to build an army of their own. The story widens to the organisation that watches the Drifters, the Octobrist sorcerers, and to the Ends' army of monsters marching from the north. The later volumes follow a great war between the two sides, with figures such as Hannibal, Scipio and Butch Cassidy fighting among the Drifters.

Adaptations

Hoods Drifters Studio's anime (2016) adapted the early volumes in twelve episodes, followed by OVAs.

Reading it today

Still officially running, but very slowly, with seven volumes by 2023. Our glossary entry on isekai explains the genre it twists, and our entry on Kōta Hirano covers Hellsing.

title: Trigun
synopsis: On a desert planet, a gunman with a sixty-billion-double-dollar bounty on his head turns out to be a clumsy, cheerful pacifist hiding a terrible past. The title reduces to 8 — the ledger.
body:
8Eight — power. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Yasuhiro Nightow's Trigun began in Tokuma Shoten's Monthly Shōnen Captain in 1995. When that magazine closed, it continued as Trigun Maximum in Shōnen Gahōsha's Young King OURs until 2007. It is set on a desert planet, settled long ago by colonists from Earth.

The story

Vash the Stampede, the "Humanoid Typhoon", is said to destroy whole towns, and there is an enormous price on his head. In person he is a goofy, doughnut-loving man in a red coat who refuses to kill anyone. Two insurance agents follow him to limit the damage, and a gun-toting priest, Nicholas D. Wolfwood, joins him. Slowly the truth about Vash, the planet and his twin brother Knives comes out.

The tone

It begins as a comic space western and becomes a serious story about violence, pacifism and whether it is ever right to kill to save others.

Why it matters

It is a much-loved cult classic. Its 1998 anime was a landmark for anime abroad, and it was adapted again as Trigun Stampede in 2023.

Trigun and Trigun Maximum

The story was published in two parts. Trigun, the first three volumes, ran in Monthly Shōnen Captain from 1995 until the magazine closed in 1997, and is mostly episodic adventure. Trigun Maximum, fourteen volumes in Young King OURs from 1997 to 2007, picks up after a time skip and turns to the war between Vash and his brother Knives, the origins of the colonists' ships, and the Plants, the living power sources the colonies depend on. The two parts form one story.

Adaptations

Madhouse's 1998 anime adapted the early manga loosely and gave it its own ending, and became one of the best-known anime of its decade abroad. The film Badlands Rumble (2010) is a standalone adventure. Trigun Stampede (2023), a computer-animated reimagining, retells the story with major changes and leads into a sequel.

title: Boys Over Flowers
synopsis: A working-class girl at an elite school stands up to the four rich boys who rule it, and finds herself pursued by their arrogant leader. The title reduces to 3 — the telling.
body:
3A 3 by its title: creative communicator, and therefore the telling.

What it is

Yōko Kamio's Boys Over Flowers ran in Shueisha's Margaret from 1992 to 2003 and was collected in thirty-seven volumes. Its Japanese title, Hana Yori Dango, is a pun on a proverb meaning "dumplings rather than flowers", the practical over the pretty.

The story

Tsukushi Makino comes from a poor family, but her parents have sent her to Eitoku Academy, a school for the very rich. The school is ruled by the F4, four wealthy boys led by the violent, spoiled Tsukasa Dōmyōji, who bully anyone they mark with a red card. When Tsukushi defends a friend and is targeted, she fights back. To everyone's surprise, Tsukasa falls for her.

The story's appeal

It is a Cinderella story with a heroine who refuses to be grateful. Tsukushi's stubbornness, the extravagant wealth of the F4 and the long, stormy romance, which faces Tsukasa's formidable mother, kept readers hooked for a decade.

Why it matters

It is one of the most successful shōjo manga ever, and one of the most adapted: an anime in 1996, Japanese television dramas, and celebrated versions in Taiwan as Meteor Garden and in South Korea. A sequel, Boys Over Flowers Season 2, followed on Shōnen Jump+.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are Tsukushi's war with the F4 and her confused feelings for Rui Hanazawa, the quietest of them. Her relationship with Tsukasa grows through a series of trips and rivalries, against the opposition of his mother, who tries to buy her off, ruin her family and marry him to someone suitable. The last volumes follow Tsukasa's departure for New York, his memory loss after an accident, and the long road back to the couple's ending.

Adaptations

The 1996 anime was followed by an anime film (1997), Taiwan's Meteor Garden (2001), the Japanese dramas of 2005 and 2007 and their film (2008), and South Korea's 2009 drama. The sequel, Hana Nochi Hare, also known as Boys Over Flowers Season 2, set a decade later at the same school, was adapted as a drama in 2018.

title: Marmalade Boy
synopsis: When her parents divorce to swap partners with another couple, a girl must share a home with their son, a charming boy she cannot read. The title reduces to 11 — the signal.

11An 11 by its title: visionary (master 11), and therefore the signal.

What it is

Wataru Yoshizumi's Marmalade Boy ran in Shueisha's Ribon from 1992 to 1995 and was collected in eight volumes. Miki Koishikawa is a high-school student whose parents announce, cheerfully, that they are divorcing.

The story

On a holiday, Miki's parents met another couple, the Matsuuras, and each fell in love with the other's partner. The four adults decide to swap partners and all live together in one house, with their children. That brings Miki under the same roof as Yū Matsuura, a handsome, teasing boy whose sweet surface, like marmalade, hides something bitter.

The tone

It is a romantic comedy with a soap-opera twist, full of love triangles, misunderstandings and a family secret. Its fashion and lightness made it a symbol of 1990s Ribon.

Why it matters

It was one of the biggest shōjo hits of the 1990s, and its 1994 anime was very popular in Japan and abroad. A sequel, Marmalade Boy Little, follows the next generation.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are the new household and the beginnings of Miki and Yū's romance, complicated by Miki's friend Ginta, Yū's former girlfriend Arimi and a series of rivals. The middle of the series is a misunderstanding about the two families' past that seems to make their love impossible. The final volumes resolve the truth about Yū's parents.

Adaptations and sequel

Toei's anime ran for 76 episodes from 1994 to 1995, adding much original material, followed by a film. A Taiwanese drama appeared in 2002 and a Japanese live-action film in 2018. Marmalade Boy Little (2013–2018) follows Miki and Yū's younger siblings.

title: Video Girl Ai
synopsis: A heartbroken boy rents a tape from a mysterious video shop, and the girl in it steps out of the screen to cheer him up. The title reduces to 3 — the telling.
body:
3A 3 by its title: creative communicator, and therefore the telling.

What it is

Masakazu Katsura's Video Girl Ai ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1989 to 1992 and was collected in fifteen volumes. Yōta Moteuchi is a shy, kind high-school student whose name, people joke, means "unpopular". The girl he loves, Moemi, loves his best friend.

The story

Yōta finds a strange shop that only pure-hearted people can see, and rents a tape of a video girl, a girl who will comfort a lonely boy. But his video player is broken, and Ai Amano comes out of the screen different from her programming: rough, cooking badly and capable of real feelings. And her tape will only play for a limited time.

The style

Katsura's art is realistic and beautiful, with very lifelike, appealing faces and bodies, and the story treats teenage longing with seriousness. Some of it is fanservice; much more is heartbreak.

Why it matters

It was an unusually emotional romance for Jump and remains a classic. It was adapted into a live-action film and an anime in the early 1990s.

How the story is divided

Most of the series is Ai's story: her arrival, her growing feelings for Yōta, his attempts to win Moemi, and the shop's owner, Rolex, who wants to correct Ai's malfunction. It ends with the expiry of Ai's tape and what Yōta is willing to do to save her. The last two volumes are a separate story, Len's Story, about another boy and another video girl, which shows what has become of the shop.

Adaptations

A live-action film appeared in 1991 and a six-episode OVA in 1992. A television drama, Den'ei Shōjo, set years later, aired in 2012 and was followed by a second season.

title: Hayate the Combat Butler
synopsis: A boy sold to gangsters by his parents ends up as the butler of a very rich, very young girl, in a comedy packed with parodies. Filed under 9, the closing.
body:
9Title sums to 81 and reduces to 9 — The Closing, where the reference files a completion.

What it is

Kenjirō Hata's Hayate the Combat Butler ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday from 2004 to 2017 and was collected in fifty-two volumes. On Christmas Eve, sixteen-year-old Hayate Ayasaki learns that his feckless parents have sold him to the yakuza to pay off their gambling debts.

The story

Desperate, Hayate decides to kidnap someone for ransom. His target is Nagi Sanzenin, a thirteen-year-old heiress, but his clumsy speech sounds like a love confession, and when he then saves her from real kidnappers, she hires him as her butler. Hayate is unluckily kind and almost superhumanly tough, and becomes the centre of a huge cast of rich girls, maids and rivals.

The style

It is a romantic comedy packed with parodies of other manga, anime and games, along with jokes about otaku culture; Nagi herself dreams of being a manga artist.

Why it matters

Its constant references to anime, games and fan culture made it a defining comedy of the 2000s otaku boom, written for readers who recognised every joke. It was adapted into anime from 2007.

How the story is divided

For most of its run, the series is episodic: Hayate's days as Nagi's butler, life at the elite Hakuō Academy, and an ever larger cast of girls who fall for him. Longer arcs break in, most importantly a trip to Greece that reveals Hayate's childhood connection to a girl named Athena. In the second half, Nagi loses her inheritance, the household moves to a cheap apartment building, and Nagi works seriously at becoming a manga artist, before the final arc returns to Athena and the secret that ties the story together.

Adaptations

The anime ran for four seasons, by SynergySP (2007–2008), J.C.Staff (2009) and Manglobe (2012 and 2013), with a film in 2011. The manga has passed 21 million copies in circulation.

Complete in 52 volumes. The jokes are dense with references to the anime, games and manga of the 2000s, so it reads best with some knowledge of the period.

title: Beelzebub
synopsis: The toughest delinquent at the worst high school in Japan finds himself raising the infant son of the Demon King. 35 in the letters, reducing to 8.

8The letters of this title total 35, an 8 — the number of money, authority, and the machinery of ambition.

What it is

Ryūhei Tamura's Beelzebub ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2009 to 2014 and was collected in twenty-eight volumes. Tatsumi Oga is the most feared delinquent at Ishiyama High, a school full of thugs.

The story

One day, Oga sees a man floating down a river, pulls him out, and the man splits open to reveal a baby. The baby is Beelzebub IV, son of the Demon King, sent to Earth to destroy humanity, and he has chosen Oga as his parent, because Oga is so brutal. The demon maid Hilda moves in with Oga's family, and Oga, unable to get rid of the baby, has to raise him, while fighting every delinquent and demon who comes for them.

The style

It is a comic delinquent battle manga with a baby on the hero's back, mixing fights, gags and an odd but genuine father-son bond.

Why it matters

It was a popular Jump comedy of its time and an affectionate update of the delinquent genre. It was adapted into an anime in 2011.

How the story is divided

The first volumes set Oga and the baby against Ishiyama High's toughest delinquents, the Tōhōshinki. The story then moves to St. Ishiyama, an elite school where Oga's class is sent after their own is destroyed, and to fights with the Demon King's Behemoth Corps, a unit of demon soldiers sent to Earth. Later arcs bring in Beelzebub's elder brother, En, and his retinue, while the comedy and the bond between Oga and the baby continue throughout.

Adaptations

Pierrot's anime ran for 60 episodes from 2011 to 2012, ending before the manga did.

title: Makoto-chan
synopsis: Kazuo Umezu, master of horror, turns to gag manga with a grubby, wild little boy who drives his family to despair. Filed under 11, the signal.
body:
11Reduced, this title gives 11. It sits on The Signal with the rest of a signal received early.

What it is

Kazuo Umezu's Makoto-chan ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday from 1976 to 1981. It was a huge hit, and a surprise from a creator best known for horror.

The story

Makoto Sawada is a small boy with a runny nose, no shame and endless energy. Each chapter follows his disgusting, absurd and destructive adventures at home and in the neighbourhood, and the despair of his family and everyone else around him.

The style

It is wild, crude gag manga. Umezu draws it with the same intense, wide-eyed faces as his horror, which makes the jokes stranger. Makoto's hand gesture and catchphrase, gwashi, became a craze among Japanese children.

Why it matters

It showed that a master of horror could also make Japan laugh, and it is one of the classic gag manga of the 1970s. It was adapted into an anime film in 1980.

How it is organised

There is no plot: each chapter is a self-contained disaster. Makoto torments his parents, his teachers, his dog and the girl he loves, and his family's attempts to make him behave only make things worse. The humour is physical and scatological, and its timing borrows from the panic of Umezu's horror, so that a page that looks like the moment before a monster appears ends with Makoto's runny nose instead.

Its place in Umezu's work

It followed The Drifting Classroom in the same magazine, and readers who had been terrified by that grim catastrophe a few years earlier now found Umezu making them laugh. The gwashi gesture, made with the thumb, index finger and little finger, became one of the most imitated in Japanese playgrounds and stayed associated with Umezu for the rest of his life.

Reading it today

Its humour is of its time, and very crude. Readers who know Umezu only through horror should look at a few chapters to see the other half of his career. Our entry on Kazuo Umezu covers his horror classics.

title: I"s
synopsis: A shy high-school boy cannot tell the girl he loves how he feels, and the return of a childhood friend makes everything more complicated. Filed under 1, the opening.
body:

What it is

Masakazu Katsura's I"s ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1997 to 2000 and was collected in fifteen volumes. Ichitaka Seto is a high-school student in love with his classmate Iori Yoshizuki, a gentle girl who is starting to work as a model and actress. He is too awkward to say anything, and often says the opposite of what he means.

The story

The series follows Ichitaka through high school and beyond, as he tries to find the courage to confess. Complicating things is Itsuki Akiba, a lively childhood friend who returns from America, and other girls who fall for him.

The style

Katsura's realistic, beautiful character art makes the romance feel very real, and his attention to the small misunderstandings and missed chances of teenage love is precise. The title plays on the letter I, which begins the names of the main characters.

Why it matters

It is one of Jump's best-known romances and a companion to Katsura's Video Girl Ai. It was adapted into original video animations and, in 2018, a live-action television drama.

How the story is divided

The first part covers Ichitaka's second year of high school, his time with Iori at school and their slow approach towards each other, interrupted by misunderstandings and rivals. Itsuki's return from America complicates his feelings in the middle volumes. The last part follows the characters beyond high school, as Iori's acting career pulls her into the public eye and Ichitaka must finally say what he has been avoiding for years.

Adaptations

Two OVA series were made, From I"s (2002) and I"s Pure (2002–2003), and a live-action television drama in 2018.

title: Blood Blockade Battlefront
synopsis: In a New York merged overnight with another world, a young photographer with divine eyes joins a secret society that keeps the city from collapse. Filed under 9, the closing.
body:
9Reduced, this title gives 9. It sits on The Closing with the rest of a completion.

What it is

Yasuhiro Nightow's Blood Blockade Battlefront ran in Shueisha's Jump SQ from 2009 to 2015 and was collected in ten volumes, followed by a sequel. One night, New York was swallowed by a gate to the Beyond. Now it is Hellsalem's Lot, a city where humans and otherworldly beings live side by side, sealed from the outside world by a mysterious fog.

The story

Leonardo Watch is a young man who came to the city after a strange being gave him the All-Seeing Eyes of the Gods, at the cost of his younger sister's sight. He joins Libra, a secret organisation led by the gentle giant Klaus von Reinherz, whose members fight with blood-based techniques to stop the city's disasters from spreading to the rest of the world.

The style

It is a series of short, explosive stories in an overwhelmingly busy city, drawn with Nightow's dense, kinetic art and full of odd monsters, gangsters and gadgets.

Why it matters

It is Nightow's major work after Trigun. Its 2015 anime by Bones was popular around the world.

How the story is divided

There is no single long arc. Most stories are self-contained cases for Libra: a gang war, a vampire of the most dangerous kind, an underground game, a city-wide catastrophe averted at the last minute. A few threads run through the whole, among them Leonardo's search for a way to restore his sister's sight and the Blood Breeds, ancient vampires whom only Klaus can seal.

Sequels and adaptations

title: Fly Me to the Moon
synopsis: A boy is saved from a truck by a mysterious girl, proposes on the spot, and she agrees, in a comedy about a young newly married couple. Filed under 6, the care.
body:
6The letters of this title total 69, a 6 — the number of care, community, and the weight of duty.

What it is

Kenjirō Hata's Fly Me to the Moon has run in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday since 2018. Nasa Yuzaki, a brilliant boy named after the space agency, is hit by a truck while chasing a beautiful girl he has just seen. She saves him, and with his last strength he asks her to go out with him.

The story

She agrees, on one condition: they must be married. Years later, on his eighteenth birthday, the girl, Tsukasa, appears at his door with a marriage form. The series follows their life as a young married couple, learning about each other, while the mystery of Tsukasa's past slowly unfolds.

The tone

Unlike most romantic comedies, it skips the will-they-won't-they and begins with the marriage. The comedy comes from small domestic moments, and the couple's affection is sweet and open.

Why it matters

It is a popular example of the newly-married romance. It was adapted into anime from 2020.

The mystery underneath

Behind the domestic comedy, the series slowly reveals who Tsukasa is and why she was willing to marry a stranger. The answer draws on The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, Japan's oldest surviving story, about a princess from the moon, and turns the romance into a story about time and mortality. Readers who want only the sweetness can enjoy it as that; readers who want the mystery will find clues from the first volume.

Adaptations and the creator

The anime began in 2020, followed by a special episode and a second season in 2023. Kenjirō Hata is also the creator of Hayate the Combat Butler, a long-running comedy about a boy who becomes a rich girl's butler, and his love of parody and references shows in both. The title comes from the jazz standard of the same name.

title: Blood on the Tracks
synopsis: A quiet boy's devoted mother does something terrible on a summer hike, and his life becomes a slow struggle to understand her. Read from the signal, as an 11.
body:
11An 11 by its title: visionary (master 11), and therefore the signal.

What it is

Shūzō Oshimi's Blood on the Tracks ran in Shogakukan's Big Comic Superior from 2017 to 2023 and was collected in seventeen volumes. Seiichi Osabe is a shy middle-school boy in a small town in Gunma. His mother, Seiko, is beautiful, gentle and devoted to him, perhaps too devoted.

The story

During a family hike in the mountains, Seiichi's cousin plays at the edge of a cliff. Seiko pushes him off. Seiichi sees it, and she knows he has seen it. From then on he is caught in her world, unable to tell anyone, as she pulls him closer and away from friends and from a girl who likes him.

The style

Oshimi uses long, wordless sequences, extreme close-ups of faces and the sound of cicadas to build unbearable tension. The story follows Seiichi far into adulthood.

Why it matters

It is a devastating psychological study of control, love and the parent-child bond, and many readers consider it Oshimi's masterpiece.

How the story is divided

The first part covers Seiichi's middle-school years after the cliff: the police investigation, his cousin's injuries and the long months in which Seiko pulls him away from everyone else, including Fukiishi, a girl who likes him. The second part jumps decades forward to Seiichi as a lonely adult, living alone, until Seiko returns to his life. The last volumes follow the two of them to the end of her life, and to whether Seiichi can understand what was done to him.

Reading it today

Complete in 17 volumes. It is a hard read; Oshimi stretches single moments across many pages. Our entry on The Flowers of Evil covers his earlier work.

title: Ceres, Celestial Legend
synopsis: On her sixteenth birthday, a girl learns she carries the spirit of a celestial maiden, and that her own family intends to kill her for it. The title reduces to 3 — the telling.

What it is

Yuu Watase's Ceres, Celestial Legend ran in Shogakukan's Shōjo Comic from 1996 to 2000 and was collected in fourteen volumes. It draws on the Japanese legend of the tennyo, a celestial maiden who comes down to Earth and is trapped there when a man steals her feathered robe.

The story

On their sixteenth birthday, Aya Mikage and her twin brother Aki are summoned by their wealthy grandfather. Aya, it turns out, is a descendant of the celestial maiden, whose angry spirit, Ceres, is awakening in her. The Mikage family, descended from the man who stole the robe, decides she must die. Aya escapes, helped by a mysterious young man, Tōya, and searches for the robe, while Ceres takes over her body and Aki is drawn to the other side.

The tone

It is darker and more adult than Watase's Fushigi Yūgi, a supernatural thriller about family, inheritance and the control of women's bodies, with a powerful romance at its centre.

Why it matters

It is one of Watase's most admired works. It was adapted into anime in 2000.

How the story is divided

The first volumes follow Aya's flight from her family, the other descendants of celestial maidens who are being hunted, and her growing love for Tōya, who has no memory of his past. The middle of the series reveals what the Mikage family are doing with the maiden's power, and Aki's possession by the spirit of the man who stole the robe. The last volumes are the search for the robe and the confrontation between the maiden's anger and the people who wronged her.

Adaptations

Pierrot's anime (2000) adapted the whole manga in 24 episodes.

title: Full Moon o Sagashite
synopsis: A twelve-year-old girl with a tumour in her throat wants to be a singer, and two shinigami give her a healthy, older body for the time she has left. The title reduces to 5 — the turn.

What it is

Arina Tanemura's Full Moon o Sagashite, "Searching for the Full Moon", ran in Shueisha's Ribon from 2002 to 2004 and was collected in seven volumes. Mitsuki Kōyama is twelve and lives with her strict grandmother. She has a tumour in her throat, and refuses an operation because it could take her voice.

The story

Two shinigami, Takuto and Meroko, come to watch over her, because she has only a year to live. When they see how much she wants to sing, Takuto lets her transform into a healthy sixteen-year-old, and as "Full Moon" she enters a singing contest and becomes a star. Her dream is also to see again a boy she loved, who moved to America.

The tone

It is a magical-girl story built on illness and death. Tanemura's art is ornate and sparkling, but the story is about grief, depression and the choice to live.

Why it matters

It is one of Tanemura's best-loved works. It was adapted into anime in 2002.

How the story is divided

The first volumes follow Mitsuki's double life as Full Moon, her rise as a singer and her friendship with Takuto, a shinigami who was himself once a musician. The middle of the series reveals what happened to Eichi, the boy she wants to see again, and the story behind Takuto and Meroko. The last volumes deal with Mitsuki's illness and her grandmother's grief, and end with her decision about the operation that could save her life and take her voice.

Adaptations

Studio Deen's anime ran for 52 episodes from 2002 to 2003. It runs ahead of the manga and changes the story.

title: Shadow Star
synopsis: A cheerful girl befriends a star-shaped creature on a summer island, and discovers other children whose creatures are terrible weapons. 38 in the letters, reducing to 11.

What it is

Mohiro Kitoh's Shadow Star, known in Japan as Narutaru, ran in Kodansha's Afternoon from 1998 to 2003 and was collected in twelve volumes. Shiina Tamai is a lively twelve-year-old girl. On a summer visit to the seaside, she nearly drowns and is saved by a strange, star-shaped creature she names Hoshimaru.

The story

Back home, she learns that other children also have such creatures, called shadow dragons, which obey their wishes. Some of those children are lonely, abused or furious, and use their dragons to kill. Shiina is drawn into a growing conflict between children who want to remake or end the world.

The tone

It starts like a gentle children's adventure and becomes extremely violent and despairing, with scenes of abuse and cruelty. It deliberately overturns the idea of the child with a magical friend.

Why it matters

It is a notorious, influential work of dark seinen science fiction, and the forerunner of Kitoh's Bokurano. It was adapted into an anime in 2003, which covered only the gentler early part.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are Shiina's summer with Hoshimaru and her discovery of the other children and their dragons, among them Akira, who becomes her friend, and the cruel and lonely Hiroko. The middle of the series follows a group of children who plan to destroy humanity, and a government that tries to use the dragons for its own ends. The last volumes reveal what the dragons are, and end on a scale of destruction the opening chapters never hinted at.

Adaptations

The 2003 anime adapted only the first part of the story, and stops before its darkest turns.

Reading it today

Complete in twelve volumes, and very disturbing in places. Our entry on Bokurano covers Kitoh's later series on similar themes.

title: Crows
synopsis: A good-natured, unbeatable fighter transfers to the roughest boys' school in Japan, where no one has ever brought the delinquents together. Filed under 6, the care.
body:

What it is

Hiroshi Takahashi's Crows ran in Akita Shoten's Monthly Shōnen Champion from 1990 to 1998 and was collected in twenty-six volumes. Suzuran All-Boys High School is called "the school of crows": a place so full of delinquents and gangs that no one has ever managed to rule it.

The story

Harumichi Bōya transfers to Suzuran. He is a monster in a fight, but he is also cheerful, kind to the weak and uninterested in becoming boss. As he clashes with Suzuran's factions and with rival schools and gangs, he becomes a legend almost without trying.

The style

It is a classic delinquent manga, with big fights, loyalty, honour among rivals and a dry humour. Takahashi's world grew into a huge shared setting, continued in the sequel Worst.

Why it matters

It is one of the most influential delinquent manga. It inspired Takashi Miike's film Crows Zero in 2007, an original story set at Suzuran, which was a big hit.

How the story is divided

The series is a chain of arcs, each built around a new opponent. Harumichi arrives at Suzuran and meets the friends who will follow him, then clashes with the school's factions and with rival schools. Later arcs bring in motorcycle gangs and older delinquents, and the story ends with Harumichi's graduation and the generation after him taking over.

Adaptations and sequel

Takahashi continued the setting in Worst (2001–2013), set at Suzuran in a later generation. Takashi Miike's Crows Zero (2007) and Crows Zero II (2009), and Crows Explode (2014), tell original stories, and the setting later crossed over with the HiGH&LOW franchise.

title: Bungo Stray Dogs
altTitles: 文豪ストレイドッグス
synopsis: In Yokohama, a young orphan who turns into a tiger joins a detective agency whose members, named after great writers, have supernatural abilities. The title reduces to 7 — the inquiry.
body:
7A 7 by its title: analyst & seeker, and therefore the inquiry.

What it is

Bungo Stray Dogs, written by Kafka Asagiri and drawn by Sango Harukawa, has run in Kadokawa's Young Ace since 2012. Its characters are named after real Japanese and foreign writers, the bungō or literary greats, and each has a supernatural ability named after one of that writer's works.

The story

Atsushi Nakajima has been thrown out of his orphanage and is starving in Yokohama. He saves a man trying to drown himself, Osamu Dazai, who turns out to be a member of the Armed Detective Agency, a group of ability users who take the cases the police cannot. Atsushi, it turns out, can turn into a white tiger, and he joins the agency. Its great rival is the Port Mafia, whose fearsome Ryūnosuke Akutagawa becomes Atsushi's enemy.

The style

It mixes action, comedy and detective stories, with stylish characters and many playful literary references. Later arcs bring in foreign writers, such as Fyodor Dostoevsky.

Why it matters

It is a hit franchise with anime from 2016, films and stage plays. It has inspired many readers to look up the real writers, and the city of Yokohama has worked with it on promotions.

How the story is divided

The first volumes introduce the Armed Detective Agency and its war with the Port Mafia. The story then widens as the Guild, an organisation of American writers led by F. Scott Fitzgerald, invades Yokohama, forcing the agency and the mafia into an alliance. The Decay of the Angel arc, led by Fyodor Dostoevsky, frames the agency for terrorism and sets the whole city against it, and later arcs follow its members in prison, on the run and inside the government. The Dark Era and Fifteen stories, about Dazai's past in the mafia, are told in novels and spin-offs.

Adaptations

Bones' anime ran for five seasons from 2016 to 2023, with the film Dead Apple (2018). The manga has passed 28 volumes and 16 million copies.

The manga is still running and well ahead of the anime.

title: Air Gear
synopsis: A street-fighting teenager discovers Air Treks, motorised inline skates that let riders leap between rooftops, and sets out to rule the skies. Filed under 5, the turn.

What it is

Oh! great's Air Gear ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2002 to 2012 and was collected in thirty-seven volumes. In its near-future Japan, the craze is Air Treks: motorised inline skates that let riders race, fight and leap between buildings.

The story

Itsuki "Ikki" Minami is a cocky middle-school fighter who lives with four sisters, the Noyamano girls, who turn out to be legendary Air Trek riders. After a humiliating defeat by a rider gang, Ikki takes up Air Treks himself and forms his own team, aiming to climb to the top of a hierarchy of riders and to master the mysterious Regalia that rule it.

The style

Oh! great is famous for extremely detailed, dynamic art. The series' action is fast and vertical, with impossible tricks drawn in dense panels, and it also includes a good deal of fanservice.

Why it matters

It turned extreme sport into battle manga, with a pair of skates as the power system, and its art is among the most technically ambitious in 2000s shōnen. It was adapted into an anime in 2006.

How the story is divided

The early volumes follow Ikki's first battles and the founding of his team, Kogarasumaru, with his school friends. The team climbs through matches against other teams in the Parts War, a ranked system of battles for emblems. The middle of the series introduces the Sky Regalia and the Kings who hold them, and Ikki's rivalry with them. The final arcs reveal the scientific project behind Air Treks and the Trophaeum Tower, and become a war for control of the regalia and of the sky itself.

Adaptations

Toei's anime (2006) adapted the early arcs in 25 episodes, and three OVAs, Kuro no Hane to Nemuri no Mori, followed in 2010 and 2011.

title: Tenjho Tenge
synopsis: Two cocky delinquents enrol at a high school built around martial arts, and are drawn into a centuries-old war between fighting clans. Filed under 6, the care.

What it is

Oh! great's Tenjho Tenge ran in Shueisha's Ultra Jump from 1997 to 2010 and was collected in twenty-two volumes. Sōichirō Nagi and his friend Bob Makihara are street fighters who arrive at Tōdō Academy planning to take over the school.

The story

They discover that Tōdō is a school devoted to martial arts, where student clubs fight for power. After they are crushed by the Juken Club and its leader Maya Natsume, they join it. Its rival, the student council's Executive Council, has ambitions that reach back to a history of feuding clans, and the series turns to a long flashback about the fighters of the previous generation.

The style

Oh! great's art is extremely detailed and dynamic, with intricate, realistic martial-arts moves. The series is also known for heavy fanservice and violence, which some editions toned down.

Why it matters

It established Oh! great as one of manga's most technically admired artists, before Air Gear. It was adapted into an anime in 2004.

How the story is divided

The first volumes follow Nagi and Bob's arrival at Tōdō Academy, their defeat by the Juken Club and their training. A long flashback then tells the story of the previous generation, Maya and her brother Shin, and the tragedy that split the school. The later volumes return to the present, as the conflict between the clubs grows into a war between ancient clans and reveals Nagi's own place in their history.

What it is

Tsukasa Hōjō's Cat's Eye ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1981 to 1985 and was collected in eighteen volumes. It was Hōjō's first series, before City Hunter.

The story

Hitomi, Rui and Ai Kisugi run a café called Cat's Eye. In secret, they are also Cat's Eye, the famous phantom thieves who announce their heists with a calling card. Their targets are the paintings of their father, an artist who disappeared, and whose collection was scattered; they hope the paintings will lead them to him.

The joke

The detective in charge of catching Cat's Eye is Toshio Utsumi, Hitomi's boyfriend, who often drinks coffee in their café without suspecting a thing. The series plays this for comedy and romance as much as suspense.

Why it matters

It is a classic phantom-thief story, with stylish heists and three glamorous heroines, and helped make the female thief a manga favourite. It was adapted into anime in 1983 and into a live-action film in 1997.

How the story is divided

Most chapters are self-contained heists, each built around a painting from their father's collection and a new way of fooling Toshio and the police. Over the series, the sisters come closer to learning what happened to their father, Toshio comes closer to the truth about Hitomi, and the final chapters bring both questions to their ending.

Adaptations

TMS Entertainment's anime ran for two seasons, 73 episodes, from 1983 to 1985. A live-action film followed in 1997, and the sisters returned in the animated film City Hunter: Shinjuku Private Eyes (2019). Liden Films' new anime was released on Disney+ in 2025 and 2026, and a French live-action series began in 2024.
