title: Billy Bat
synopsis: A comic artist in 1949 discovers that his cartoon bat has been drawn before, and is pulled into a conspiracy spanning the whole of human history. 29 in the letters, reducing to 11.
body:
11Title sums to 29 and reduces to 11 — The Signal, where the reference files a signal received early.

What it is

Billy Bat, by Naoki Urasawa with Takashi Nagasaki, ran in Kodansha's Morning from 2008 to 2016 and was collected in twenty volumes. It begins in 1949, with Kevin Yamagata, a Japanese-American comic artist in New York who draws a hit detective comic starring a bat, Billy Bat.

The story

When Kevin learns that the same bat was drawn in Japan before him, he goes there to find out whether he copied it, and finds himself caught in a murder. Soon it becomes clear that the bat image has appeared throughout history, and that whoever draws it can glimpse the future and change events. The story moves through the Shimoyama incident, the Kennedy assassination, the Moon landing and far beyond.

The style

It is Urasawa at his most ambitious: a conspiracy thriller across centuries, full of real events, and a story about the power of drawing and storytelling. It includes pages of the in-story Billy Bat comic itself.

Why it matters

It is one of Urasawa's most ambitious thrillers, and his most direct meditation on manga as a form.

How the story is divided

The first volumes follow Kevin Yamagata in postwar America and Japan, and his discovery of the bat's history. The story then moves backwards and forwards in time: to earlier centuries, where the bat has been seen before; to Dallas in 1963, where the bat plays a part in Kennedy's assassination; and to the future, where the bat's power to shape history is fought over by those who want to rule with it. The final volumes are about whether anyone can draw a different ending.

Reading it today

Complete in 20 volumes. It has never been published in English, so many readers outside Japan know it through the French edition. Our entry on Naoki Urasawa covers his other thrillers.

title: Tegami Bachi
synopsis: In a land of perpetual night lit by an artificial sun, a boy becomes a Letter Bee, delivering mail across monster-filled wilds. The title reduces to 6 — the care.
body:
6A 6 by its title: nurturer & harmonizer, and therefore the care.

What it is

Hiroyuki Asada's Tegami Bachi, "Letter Bee", began in Shueisha's Weekly Shōnen Jump in 2006, moved to Jump SQ in 2007 and ended in 2015, with twenty volumes. Amberground is a land of endless night. Only the capital is lit by an artificial sun, and the farther from it you go, the darker and poorer it becomes.

The story

Lag Seeing is a boy who, as a child, was "delivered" as a parcel by a Letter Bee, Gauche Suede, who became his hero. Years later Lag becomes a Letter Bee himself. Bees deliver letters through wild lands full of huge armoured insects called Gaichū, which they fight with guns that fire fragments of their own heart and memories.

The tone

It is gentle and melancholy. Letters carry people's feelings, and each delivery is a small story about love and loss. Over time it reveals darker truths about the sun and the government.

Why it matters

It is a distinctive, beautifully drawn fantasy, and was adapted into an anime in 2009.

How the story is divided

The early chapters are Lag's deliveries with his dingo, Niche, a strange girl with the strength of a beast, and his search for Gauche, who has disappeared. The story deepens when Lag finds Gauche again, without his memories, working for Reverse, a group that attacks Letter Bees and seeks revenge on the government. The final volumes reveal the secret of Amberground's artificial sun, what it is made of, and what it has cost the people who live under it.

Adaptations

Pierrot's anime ran for two seasons, Tegami Bachi (2009–2010) and Tegami Bachi Reverse (2010–2011), ending before the manga.

Reading it today

Complete in 20 volumes. The anime ends with its own conclusion, so the manga is the only place for the full story.

title: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid
altTitles: 小林さんちのメイドラゴン
synopsis: A tired office worker gets drunk, invites a dragon home, and wakes up to find her standing at the door as a devoted maid. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4Four — foundation. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

coolkyousinnjya's Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid has run in Futabasha's Monthly Action since 2013. Kobayashi is a programmer in her twenties, practical, overworked and fond of maids. One night, drunk in the mountains, she pulls a sword from a dragon's back and invites it to stay with her.

The story

The next morning, the dragon, Tohru, appears at her apartment in the form of a young woman in a maid's outfit, ready to serve. Kobayashi lets her stay. Soon other dragons arrive from their world, including the small, solemn Kanna, who starts primary school, and Kobayashi's apartment becomes a home for a strange, growing family.

The tone

It is a gentle comedy about everyday life and found family. Under the slapstick and dragon chaos, it is about loneliness, what it means to belong and the difference between human and dragon lifespans.

Why it matters

Its 2017 anime by Kyoto Animation made it a worldwide hit, and it has spun off several manga by other artists.

The cast

Tohru is followed into the human world by other dragons from opposing factions: Kanna, a young dragon exiled for her pranks; Lucoa, a former goddess who lives with a boy magician; Fafnir, a misanthropic hoarder who becomes an obsessive gamer; Elma, Tohru's rival, who takes an office job at Kobayashi's company; and later Ilulu, who arrives as an enemy. Each chapter is a small domestic story, and the humour comes from vast, ancient beings learning to do laundry, go to school and hold down jobs.

Adaptations and spin-offs

Kyoto Animation's anime (2017) made the series a worldwide hit. Its second season (2021) was completed after the 2019 arson attack on the studio, which killed the first season's director, Yasuhiro Takemoto, among others. Spin-off manga by other artists include Kanna's Daily Life, Elma's Office Life and Fafnir the Recluse.

title: Hi Score Girl
synopsis: In 1991, a boy who lives for arcade games is beaten at Street Fighter II by a rich, silent girl, and a long rivalry turns into something more. The title reduces to 6 — the care.
body:
6A 6 by its title: nurturer & harmonizer, and therefore the care.

What it is

Rensuke Oshikiri's Hi Score Girl ran in Square Enix's Monthly Big Gangan from 2010 to 2018 and was collected in ten volumes. It begins in 1991, at the height of Japan's arcade boom. Haruo Yaguchi is a sixth-grader who is bad at school and lives for video games.

The story

At his local arcade, Haruo is humiliated at Street Fighter II by Akira Ōno, a wealthy, perfect classmate who never speaks. Gaming is her only escape from a strict family. Their rivalry grows across the years of middle and high school into a slow-burning love story, with another girl, Koharu, also falling for Haruo.

The style

The series is a love letter to 1990s games, with real titles, characters and arcade culture shown in loving detail. Akira's silence means everything is said through expression and action.

Why it matters

It is an unusual romance and a portrait of a gaming generation. It was adapted into an anime in 2018.

How the story is divided

The first part covers Haruo and Akira's elementary-school years, built around arcade games of 1991 and 1992, from Street Fighter II to Final Fight. Akira is then sent to study in America, and the middle part is Haruo's middle-school years with Koharu, who loves him and learns to play to be near him. The last part follows the three into high school and the rise of 3D fighting games, and ends with Haruo's choice.

Adaptations

J.C.Staff's anime ran for two seasons (2018 and 2019) and adapted the whole manga. The series was briefly suspended in 2014 over the use of games' characters without permission, a dispute that was settled the following year.

Reading it today

Complete in ten volumes. Readers who played the games of the period will catch many more references.

title: Ushio and Tora
synopsis: A temple boy frees a monstrous yōkai pinned in his cellar for five hundred years, and the two become reluctant partners against a great evil. Read from the opening, as a 1.
body:
1A 1 by its title: leader & pioneer, and therefore the opening.

What it is

Kazuhiro Fujita's Ushio and Tora ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday from 1990 to 1996 and was collected in thirty-three volumes. Ushio Aotsuki is a hot-headed boy whose father is a priest at an old temple.

The story

In the temple's cellar, Ushio finds a huge, tiger-like yōkai pinned to the wall by a spear, where it has been trapped for five hundred years. He pulls out the spear, the Beast Spear, and the yōkai swears to eat him. Ushio names it Tora, "tiger", and the two set off together, fighting monsters across Japan. The spear gives Ushio great power but slowly turns its wielder into a beast, and the true enemy is the ancient evil Hakumen no Mono.

The style

Fujita's art is rough, energetic and full of motion. The series mixes humour, horror and huge battles, and its central bond, between a boy and a monster who will not admit he cares, is its heart.

Why it matters

It is a beloved classic of yōkai battle manga. It was adapted into original video animations in the 1990s and a television anime in 2015.

How the story is divided

The first volumes are episodes: Ushio and Tora fight a different yōkai each time, and those they help become allies. The middle of the series sends Ushio across Japan to find his mother, and to the yōkai of the far north, who distrust him as the wielder of the Beast Spear. The final volumes are the war with Hakumen no Mono, in which every ally Ushio has made returns, and the truth about Tora's past and the spear is revealed.

Adaptations

OVAs adapted parts of the story from 1992 to 1993. MAPPA and Studio VOLN's television anime (2015–2016) adapted the whole manga in 39 episodes, compressing many episodes along the way.

Reading it today

Complete in 33 volumes. The anime's compression means the manga's early episodes, and the allies they introduce, are richer on the page.

title: Karakuri Circus
synopsis: A boy hunted for his inheritance, a martial artist who cannot stop laughing and a puppeteer with a fighting marionette are drawn into a war against killer automata. Filed under 1, the opening.
body:
1Reduced, this title gives 1. It sits on The Opening with the rest of a first move.

What it is

Kazuhiro Fujita's Karakuri Circus ran in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday from 1997 to 2006 and was collected in forty-three volumes. Masaru Saiga is a timid boy who has inherited a fortune, and his relatives have sent killers after him.

The story

He is rescued by Narumi Katō, a martial artist with a strange illness: if he does not make children laugh, he cannot breathe. They are joined by Shirogane, a silent young woman who fights with a giant marionette. Masaru is drawn into a centuries-old war between puppeteers and the Automata, mechanical beings who spread a deadly disease and feed on human blood.

The style

It is an enormous, tangled epic that moves between characters, continents and centuries, full of grotesque automata, circus spectacle, tragedy and humour.

Why it matters

It is Fujita's longest and most ambitious work, and many readers consider it his masterpiece. It was adapted into an anime in 2018.

How the story is divided

The series alternates between two storylines, shown side by side for much of its length. One follows Masaru, who joins a travelling circus and learns to fight with a marionette of his own. The other follows Narumi, who after losing Masaru joins the Shiroganes, puppeteers who have fought the Automata across Europe for two hundred years. The two stories are joined by the history of the Automata, revealed in a long flashback to eighteenth-century China and Europe, and the final volumes bring every survivor together for a last battle.

Adaptations

Studio VOLN's anime (2018–2019) adapted the whole story in 36 episodes, compressing it heavily.

Reading it today

Complete in 43 volumes. The anime's compression leaves out much of what makes the manga loved, so readers should go to the source. Our entry on Ushio and Tora covers Fujita's first long series.

title: The Seven Deadly Sins
synopsis: A runaway princess searches for a legendary band of disgraced knights to free her kingdom, and finds their captain running a tavern on a giant pig's back. The title reduces to 3 — the telling.
body:
3Three — expression. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Nakaba Suzuki's The Seven Deadly Sins ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2012 to 2020 and was collected in forty-one volumes. It is set in a world inspired by Arthurian legend and European fantasy.

The story

The Seven Deadly Sins were the kingdom of Liones' most powerful knights, until they were accused of plotting against the king and scattered. Ten years later, the Holy Knights have seized power. Princess Elizabeth escapes to find the Sins and ask for help, and meets Meliodas, a boyish tavern owner whose bar travels on the back of a giant pig, Hawk's mother. He is the Sins' captain, the Dragon's Sin of Wrath.

The style

It is a classic team adventure: gathering the scattered Sins one by one, each with their own crime and power, and then facing ever bigger enemies, including the ancient Demon Clan.

Why it matters

It was one of the biggest shōnen hits of the 2010s, with a long anime from 2014. Its sequel, Four Knights of the Apocalypse, follows the next generation.

How the story is divided

The first part gathers the Sins one by one, each named for a sin and an animal: Meliodas the Dragon, Diane the Serpent, Ban the Fox, King the Grizzly, Gowther the Goat, Merlin the Boar and Escanor the Lion, and ends with the fall of the Holy Knights who took over Liones. The middle of the series turns to the Ten Commandments, the Demon Clan's elite warriors, and the secret of Meliodas's past. The last part is the Holy War between the clans, which resolves the curse that binds Meliodas and Elizabeth.

Adaptations and sequel

The anime began in 2014 and ran for several seasons, reaching an international audience through Netflix, and several animated films followed. The sequel manga, Four Knights of the Apocalypse, began in 2021 in the same magazine and follows a new generation, including Meliodas's son; its anime started in 2023. Suzuki's earlier series, Kongō Banchō, is a delinquent battle manga.
